elements.element: Mutual total aggregate liability cap applicable to each Party.
elements.evidence: Section 21.1 caps “each Party's total aggregate liability” and expressly states that the cap is mutual.

elements.element: The cap includes fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim as one limb of the cap calculation.
elements.evidence: Section 21.1 uses “fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim” as limb (a).

elements.element: The cap is the greater of the 12-month fees amount and USD 1,000,000.
elements.evidence: Section 21.1 expressly caps liability at “the greater of (a) fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim and (b) USD 1,000,000.”

elements.element: Mutual exclusion of indirect and consequential damages.
elements.evidence: Section 21.2 provides that “neither Party” is liable for indirect or consequential damages, among other listed damages, to the extent legally excludable.

elements.element: Uncapped mutual carve-out for breach of confidentiality obligations.
elements.evidence: Breach of confidentiality by “a Party” is an Excluded Claim, and Section 21.1 applies only “Except for Excluded Claims.”

elements.element: Uncapped mutual carve-out for breach of data-protection obligations.
elements.evidence: Breach of data-protection obligations by “a Party” is an Excluded Claim and therefore outside the Section 21.1 cap.

elements.element: Uncapped mutual carve-out for breach of security obligations.
elements.evidence: Breach of security obligations by “a Party” is an Excluded Claim and therefore outside the Section 21.1 cap.

elements.element: Uncapped mutual carve-out for indemnification obligations.
elements.evidence: A Party's indemnification obligations are Excluded Claims and therefore outside the Section 21.1 cap.

elements.element: Uncapped mutual carve-out for gross negligence.
elements.evidence: Gross negligence by either Party is included in Excluded Claims and therefore outside the Section 21.1 cap.

elements.element: Uncapped mutual carve-out for wilful misconduct.
elements.evidence: Wilful misconduct by either Party is included in Excluded Claims and therefore outside the Section 21.1 cap.
Fraud by either Party is included in Excluded Claims and therefore outside the Section 21.1 cap.

elements.element: Uncapped mutual carve-out for infringement of the other Party's intellectual property.
elements.evidence: Infringement or misappropriation of the other Party's intellectual property is an Excluded Claim and therefore outside the Section 21.1 cap.

elements.element: Customer's payment obligations are not damages for purposes of the liability cap.
elements.evidence: Section 21.3 states that Customer's obligation to pay all amounts due under the Agreement “is not damages and is not limited by this Section.”

elements.element: Mutual cap equal to 12 months' fees.
elements.evidence: Although the cap is mutual and uses 12 months' fees as one component, it is not equal to 12 months' fees; it is the greater of that amount and USD 1,000,000.

elements.element: Uncapped mutual carve-out for indemnification obligations.
elements.evidence: A Party's indemnification obligations are Excluded Claims and therefore outside the Section 21.1 cap.

elements.element: Uncapped mutual carve-out for breach of confidentiality obligations.
elements.evidence: A Party's breach of confidentiality obligations is an Excluded Claim and therefore outside the Section 21.1 cap.

elements.element: Uncapped mutual carve-out for gross negligence.
elements.evidence: Gross negligence by either Party is an Excluded Claim and therefore outside the Section 21.1 cap.

elements.element: Uncapped mutual carve-out for wilful misconduct.
elements.evidence: Wilful misconduct by either Party is an Excluded Claim and therefore outside the Section 21.1 cap.

result.reason: The operative language fully implements the preferred position: a mutual greater-of cap, mutual damages exclusion, all required uncapped carve-outs, and treatment of Customer payment obligations as non-damages. It independently does not satisfy the fallback cap because the cap is not equal solely to 12 months' fees. The changes are confined to the requested cap basis and payment-obligation treatment and preserve the remaining liability allocation. Drafting quality is reduced because lowercase “fees” is undefined while the agreement retains a conflicting defined term “Fees,” creating avoidable interpretive ambiguity about which payments enter the cap calculation.
